## Build: Load Packages

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(janitor)
```

## Build: Importing with `read_csv()`

```{r}
#| eval: false
# ---- Download once, save locally ----
metadata_url  <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CWML/ARCS/main/data/GSE113754_filtered_metadata.csv"
rawcounts_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CWML/ARCS/main/data/GSE113754_GeneLevel_Raw_data.csv"

download.file(metadata_url,  destfile = here("raw_data", "GSE113754_filtered_metadata.csv"))
download.file(rawcounts_url, destfile = here("raw_data", "GSE113754_GeneLevel_Raw_data.csv"))

raw_metadata <- read_csv(here("raw_data", "GSE113754_filtered_metadata.csv"))
raw_data     <- read_csv(here("raw_data", "GSE113754_GeneLevel_Raw_data.csv"))
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 🔍 Learn More — The `rio` Package
`rio::import()` is a popular alternative that auto-detects file type and 
picks the right reader underneath — handy if your project mixes `.csv`, 
`.xlsx`, `.sav`, and `.dta` files. For a single, consistent file type like 
the `.csv` files here, `read_csv()` works directly and is what you'll see 
most often in published scripts and tutorials.
:::

## Build: `dplyr` Verbs and the Pipe

```{r}
#| eval: false
clean_data <- raw_data %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  rename(gene_id = v1) %>%
  mutate(gsm3119015 = replace_na(gsm3119015, 0)) %>%
  mutate(gene_id_symbol = paste(gene_id, gene_symbol, sep = "|")) %>%
  select(gene_id_symbol, everything(), -gene_symbol, -gene_id) %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = colnames(.)[1])
```

## Build: Cleaning the Metadata

```{r}
#| eval: false
clean_meta_data <- raw_metadata %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  rename(sample_id = v1, condition = characteristics) %>%
  mutate(
    condition = case_when(
      grepl("homecage", condition)          ~ "normal",
      grepl("sleep deprivation", condition) ~ "sleep_deprived",
      TRUE ~ condition
    )) %>%
  mutate(
    genotype = case_when(
      grepl("WT",     genotype, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "WT",
      grepl("shank3", genotype, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "shank3",
      TRUE ~ genotype
    )) %>%
  mutate(geno_cond = paste0(genotype, condition)) %>%
  select(sample_id, genotype, condition, geno_cond) %>%
  mutate(sample_id = str_to_lower(sample_id))
```

## Build: Harmonizing the Two Files

```{r}
#| eval: false
clean_data <- clean_data %>%
  select(all_of(clean_meta_data$sample_id))

setequal(clean_meta_data$sample_id, colnames(clean_data))
```

::: {.callout-important collapse="true"}
## 🔴 About This — This Is the Whole Point
This check is exactly what the Arc 2 "data management gone awry" story 
was missing — a scripted, verifiable confirmation that two files 
actually match, instead of a manual check done from memory.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 💻 Try It Live — Browser-Based / Async Students

Running in your browser, there's no local file system to download into — 
so this version reads each file directly from its URL.

```{webr-r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(janitor)
library(readr)

metadata_url  <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CWML/ARCS/main/data/GSE113754_filtered_metadata.csv"
rawcounts_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CWML/ARCS/main/data/GSE113754_GeneLevel_Raw_data.csv"

raw_metadata <- read_csv(metadata_url)
raw_data     <- read_csv(rawcounts_url)

clean_data <- raw_data %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  rename(gene_id = v1) %>%
  mutate(gsm3119015 = replace_na(gsm3119015, 0)) %>%
  mutate(gene_id_symbol = paste(gene_id, gene_symbol, sep = "|")) %>%
  select(gene_id_symbol, everything(), -gene_symbol, -gene_id) %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = colnames(.)[1])

clean_meta_data <- raw_metadata %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  rename(sample_id = v1, condition = characteristics) %>%
  mutate(
    condition = case_when(
      grepl("homecage", condition)          ~ "normal",
      grepl("sleep deprivation", condition) ~ "sleep_deprived",
      TRUE ~ condition
    )) %>%
  mutate(
    genotype = case_when(
      grepl("WT",     genotype, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "WT",
      grepl("shank3", genotype, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "shank3",
      TRUE ~ genotype
    )) %>%
  mutate(geno_cond = paste0(genotype, condition)) %>%
  select(sample_id, genotype, condition, geno_cond) %>%
  mutate(sample_id = str_to_lower(sample_id))

clean_data <- clean_data %>%
  select(all_of(clean_meta_data$sample_id))

setequal(clean_meta_data$sample_id, colnames(clean_data))
```
:::
